manifest.name: Sales and Warehouse Management
manifest.summary: Quotation, Sales Orders, Delivery & Invoicing Control

views.note: no new view records; module extends sale & stock views in-place (xml_loc 870)

behavioral_notes.observation: THE BRIDGE: _action_confirm calls self.order_line._action_launch_stock_rule() BEFORE super(), which builds Procurement tuples from each consu line (_create_procurements) and runs self.env['stock.rule'].run(procurements). This is what concretely materializes the abstract 'action_confirm -> stock.picking' side-effect documented across the catalog: the procurement pull rule creates stock.move -> stock.picking, then pickings_to_confirm.action_confirm() triggers the scheduler. Pure side-effect, invisible in metadata.

On a confirmed order (state=='sale'), creating or re-quantifying lines also (re)launches procurement: create() calls _action_launch_stock_rule on sale lines; write() re-runs it with previous_product_uom_qty so increasing/decreasing ordered qty adds or back-logs delivery moves. write() also propagates commitment_date to move.date_deadline and logs decrease-quantity exception activities on impacted pickings.

Reverse direction of the bridge: delivery_status is computed from picking_ids.state (pending/started/partial/full), effective_date = first done customer picking's date_done, and qty_delivered_method becomes 'stock_move' for consu lines so qty_delivered is summed from done outgoing/incoming stock.move quantities (UoM-converted). Fulfillment progress flows stock -> sale, and drives invoice_status for delivery-policy products.

The order<->picking link is realized by stock.move.sale_line_id (indexed btree_not_null); stock.picking.sale_id is computed (stored, _auto_init creates the column directly) from move_ids.sale_line_id.order_id. _action_done / _action_synch_order auto-create zero-qty SO lines for delivered products not on the order, and _assign_picking_post_process posts a mail.message_origin_link from picking back to the originating sale.order.

Backend-only OWL widget registered as view_widgets:qty_at_date_widget; renders the green/red availability popover on SO lines from the computed forecast fields (free_qty_today, virtual_available_at_date, scheduled_date, forecast_expected_date) and opens stock.stock_forecasted_product_product_action. Also patches ProductCatalogKanbanRecord and StockValuationReport prototypes. Static asset, not in Python metadata.

information_flows: side-effect (forward): sale.order._action_confirm -> sale.order.line._action_launch_stock_rule -> stock.rule.run -> stock.move -> stock.picking (delivery order)
side-effect (backward): stock.picking.state / stock.move.quantity -> sale.order.line.qty_delivered + sale.order.delivery_status + effective_date -> invoice_status
auto_install: true -> activates whenever both sale and stock_account are installed

capabilities: Procurement Route & MTO/MTS Selection per Order Line
value_streams: Quote-to-Cash (delivery leg): confirmed sale order -> procurement -> delivery order -> goods shipped -> qty_delivered -> invoice on delivery
policies: automation: confirm/create/write on sale lines launch stock rules (procurement); picking validation back-fills qty_delivered & delivery_status
picking_policy (direct vs one) governs partial vs all-at-once shipping; security_lead/customer_lead shift procurement date_planned

classification.apqc_category: 4.0 Deliver Physical Products (3.5.4.4 Determine fulfillment process)
classification.rationale: sale_stock is THE BRIDGE that makes the chain's abstract sale.order.action_confirm -> stock.picking side-effect concrete: _action_confirm calls sale.order.line._action_launch_stock_rule, which runs the procurement stock.rule that materializes delivery moves and the delivery order. It is a pure value-chain bridge realizing outbound logistics (Operations / Outbound Logistics in Porter terms): inbound demand (confirmed sale order) is transformed into a physical delivery, and fulfillment progress (qty_delivered, delivery_status) flows back to gate invoicing. It owns no standalone business object, only inherits sale.* and stock.* to wire them; classified primary because order fulfillment / shipping is a core line activity (APQC 4.0 Deliver Physical Products; the order-line fulfillment-route decision is APQC 3.5.4.4). Depends sale + stock_account and auto_installs, confirming its bridge role rather than an independent capability.

standard_capabilities: automatic delivery-order creation on order confirmation via procurement routes
MTS / MTO / drop-ship route selection per sale order line
delivery status, effective date & expected-date computation
qty_delivered driven from stock moves (invoice on delivery)
ATP / forecasted availability widget on order lines
incoterms on order & propagated to invoice
lot/serial traceability back to sale order; delivery-slip portal PDF
typical_fits: standard confirm-order -> auto delivery order -> ship -> invoice-on-delivery flow
multi-warehouse selection from user/company default warehouse
security lead time & customer lead time shifting the scheduled date
common_gaps: carrier/shipping-connector integration (delivery module / 3rd-party, out of scope here)
bespoke ATP or allocation logic (reservation strategies)
